newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Next stop for T-bond futures at 114-24.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Next stop for T-bond futures at 114-24.

text.p: September U.S. Treasury bond futures bought a one-way ticket south Friday, swallowing the prior three sessions' gains and charting a course for 114-24/32, technicians said.

A close below the level would pave the way for another steep tumble toward 113-04, a projection based on the trendline drawn from the January 1996 high, said Terence Gabriel, technical strategist for I.D.E.A. Inc.
However, Gabriel said he expected the contract to take a breather in the 114-24/32 to 114-20/32 area, which encompasses the rising 20-day moving average and Gann support.
"The market should stabilize there and mount a recovery attempt," he said.
A subsequent countertrend bounce could take prices back up to around 115-24, Gabriel said.

David Ging, Treasury market strategist for Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, projected September bond futures would test 114-19/32, a 38.2 percent retracement of the rally from the June 30 low of 110-23/32.
From there, he saw the market stabilizing or resuming the uptrend, he said. "I don't see this as a watershed day," said Ging.
Ging noted losses have run parallel across the yield curve, implying investors are less alarmed about inflation than the one-day drop might suggest.
"If the market had thought inflation was a real threat, you'd have seen the long end lead the curve lower. You'd have seen the curve steepen," Ging said.
For today, a settlement below 115-19/32 would set the stage for further declines, said Gabriel.
At midsession, September bond futures looked likely to meet that criteria. The contract was last trading down 1-20/32 at 115-04/32.
Before the sell-off, futures established a double top on daily charts with the high registered this morning matching the previous session's peak of 116-31/32, a 1-1/2-year high.
"The market was quite overextended and certainly vulnerable to any news development," said Jim Bohan, senior financial futures strategist for Merrill Lynch Capital Markets.

The severity of the breakdown, triggered by robust July U.S. employment data and upturns in the national purchasing managers' business and price indexes, has turned oscillators negative and near sell signals, technicians said.
Bohan said he looked for a retrenchment to 114-00/32 or 113-16/32 on continued profit-taking in the aftermath of the news before an ultimate resumption of the larger uptrend.
